verdict: 2026-07-27 11:19:33 PDT — A single tested Bash library is the right, proportionate shape for this repository: Bash is already the local implementation standard, jq is already required, and behavioral rejection tests directly address the defect generator that prose-presence linters cannot. The proposed boundary is incomplete, however. It extracts several calculations but leaves other deterministic decisions unverifiable, and two public interfaces still depend on facts that exist only in prose or free text. I would keep one library, but correct these seams before implementation.

findings.title: check-plan proves internal consistency, not that the required plan was compiled
findings.locus: Design pivot — Design sketch / check-plan contract
findings.claim: The listed assertions validate only rows that happen to exist. A plan can omit a mandatory P1/P7 row—or even contain zero rows with zero totals—and still satisfy uniqueness, sums, unit resolution, and pricing. Table P emission, signal evaluation, and patch application remain deterministic prose, so the pivot retains the same unproven-property defect under a stronger-sounding guard.
findings.alternative: Make the library either compile the structural plan from the target/profile plus normalized patches, or have check-plan independently rederive the complete expected structural row set and compare it exactly. Keep only narrative fields such as omissionRisk in LLM-authored prose. Add behavioral fixtures that delete a required row, suppress a firing upgrade, or misapply a patch and require nonzero exit.
findings.win: Centralizes the remaining deterministic plan rules and eliminates an entire class of valid-looking but incomplete plans; the gate proves completeness rather than merely arithmetic consistency.

findings.title: Manifest and report commands have no canonical engine-slice input
findings.locus: Design pivot — build-manifest and check-report interfaces
findings.claim: build-manifest <plan.json> cannot know which rows slice 1 executes unless hidden-failure@L1 is either hard-coded implicitly or repeated in orchestration prose. check-report likewise cannot prove that in-slice rows are executed and out-of-slice rows are omitted. Ledger identity equality alone permits every plan row to be marked omitted, recreating a coverage seam future lenses will copy.
findings.alternative: Put the supported lens×altitude capability table in the library and have build-manifest emit one JSON envelope containing engineSlice, executable records, and the complete initial ledger classification. Make check-report validate executed/omitted states against that same table. Future slices should change this one capability table only.
findings.win: Removes three copies of slice membership—from prose, manifest selection, and report synthesis—and makes false omission or false coverage mechanically impossible.

findings.title: Mechanical adjudication is dispatched by untyped LLM/free-text data
findings.claim: The current finder schema has no claimClass field, while evidence-schema.json represents mechanicalChecks.check as an arbitrary string. Therefore the proposed adjudicate command has neither an enforced claim-class enum nor a typed mapping from a class to the relevant check. A free-text or inferred class can select the wrong table row, and an unrelated not-found result can incorrectly refute a claim; the supposedly deterministic tier still depends on an unestablished property.
findings.alternative: Define a closed claimClass enum and closed mechanical check IDs in the JSON contracts, map each supported class to its required evidence facts declaratively, and reject unsupported or mismatched combinations. Test every table row plus mismatched and unrelated-check fixtures. If slice 1 cannot establish a class mechanically, route that case directly to the judgment tier instead of claiming deterministic adjudication.
findings.win: Eliminates free-text dispatch, makes the table exhaustively testable, and removes false promote/refute paths from the precision gate future lenses will inherit.
